entries.summary: BtcMusdOracle v2 deployed: Skip BTC/USD (≤60 s), a Pyth ±10% band that only gates while Pyth is under 10 minutes old, and the MUSD leg clamped to $1.00–1.02.
entries.proves: The audited oracle (round-2 fix R2X-2: a stalled Pyth can no longer freeze liquidations for an hour) prices the new market.

entries.summary: wsMUSD v2 seeded with 1 MUSD of dead shares, deposited into the real sMUSD.
entries.proves: The ERC-4626 wrapper composes with Mezo’s live sMUSD; vesting has no instant part, so its share price never falls (round-1 B-3).

entries.summary: BorrowAccountFactory v2 deployed with the bcBTC receipt and the BorrowAccount implementation in one transaction.
entries.proves: The audited core (top-ups never capped, stale timelock raises invalidated, timelocked canary grants) fits Mezo’s 10M block gas limit.

entries.summary: Market M1 v2 created on Mezo’s official testnet Morpho Blue: MUSD loan, bcBTC collateral, BtcMusdOracle v2, AdaptiveCurveIrm, LLTV 0.77.
entries.proves: The redemption-free BTC→MUSD market is recreated permissionlessly on Mezo’s own Morpho for the audited contracts.

entries.summary: Team supplied MUSD liquidity to M1 v2.
entries.proves: Borrowers can draw MUSD from the new market from its first block.

entries.summary: Governor queued setCanaryOperator for the keeper’s canary key behind the factory’s 48-hour timelock.
entries.proves: Granting a canary operator is a timelocked raise since round-1 fix D-7; anyone executes it once due, and the keeper does.

entries.summary: vMUSD v2 created through Mezo’s own VaultV2Factory (Morpho Vault V2, MUSD asset).
entries.proves: The lending vault is a stock Morpho Vault V2 from Mezo’s factory, configured by the audited deploy script.

entries.summary: WsMusdLiquidityAdapter v2 deployed: parks idle vault MUSD in wsMUSD and refuses free force-deallocation (round-2 R2X-4).
entries.proves: Nobody can strip vMUSD’s share of wsMUSD yield by force-deallocating it for free.

entries.summary: BaserateAllocator v2 deployed: owner-less, trailing-APY decisions with a same-block guard, one buffer top-up per block, idle parked during the cooldown.
entries.proves: Round-1 B-1 and round-2 R2V-3/R2X-3 fixes are live: same-block state can no longer steer the vault.

entries.summary: vMUSD v2 seeded with 100 MUSD of dead shares, allocated straight into wsMUSD.
entries.proves: The vault is protected against first-depositor inflation from its first block.

entries.summary: Backstop v2 (bMUSD) deployed: deposits close while it holds BTC, exits pay partially or in kind, dust never ties exits to the oracle.
entries.proves: Round-1 C-1/C-3 and round-2 R2V-1/R2V-7 fixes are live: no buying in below a sale, no frozen exits.

entries.summary: Backstop v2 seeded with 1 MUSD of dead shares (mandatory since round-2 R2V-2).
entries.proves: Gross-priced deposits can’t be skewed by a donation into an empty backstop.

entries.summary: FlashLiquidator v2 deployed, bound to M1 v2 and the backstop, forwarding only each liquidation’s own proceeds (round-1 C-2).
entries.proves: Zero-capital liquidations for the new market; a 1-wei donation can’t brick contract liquidators.

entries.summary: FeeRouter v2 deployed: an ownerless 40/40/20 splitter that survives an sMUSD failure and carries bribes it can’t post (round-1 D-2/D-3).
entries.proves: Fees reach sMUSD holders, veBTC voters and the treasury without any admin, even if sMUSD changes.

entries.summary: RiskLens v2 deployed: one eth_call for oracle, market, caps, backstop solvency (available cash), liquidation depth and the redemption queue.
entries.proves: The risk dashboard reads the audited contracts; reserved exit cash is no longer counted as free (round-1 D-5).

entries.summary: vMUSD v2 made the keeper’s sentinel key a sentinel: it can only cut allocations and caps, never raise them.
entries.proves: Emergency de-risking runs unattended without giving the keeper any power to move lenders’ money into new risk.

entries.summary: Team deposited 3,000 MUSD into vMUSD v2; the liquidity adapter parked it in wsMUSD in the same transaction.
entries.proves: The audited vault takes deposits and earns at least the wsMUSD rate before the allocator lends any of it to M1.

entries.summary: Governor queued the fee switch: once the 48-hour timelock passes, origination fees go to FeeRouter v2.
entries.proves: Sending fees to sMUSD holders, veBTC voters and the treasury is a timelocked change anyone can execute once due.

entries.summary: Keeper’s first rebalance on vMUSD v2: moved a 1,000 MUSD buffer into M1 v2 so borrowers can draw from the vault.
entries.proves: The owner-less allocator runs on the audited vault from the keeper’s first pass, with no team transaction.

entries.summary: Keeper liquidated its own canary at 77.26% LTV through the FlashLiquidator at 06:38 UTC, unattended (v1 stack).
entries.proves: Liquidations run on their own: the keeper found the underwater position, sized gas for Mezo and closed it with zero capital.

entries.summary: Keeper re-armed the canary 4 minutes after its liquidation, borrowing again against the collateral left in it (v1 stack).
entries.proves: The canary loop sustains itself: open near the line, drift, get liquidated, reopen. A live liquidation test every cycle.

entries.summary: Keeper opened its own canary at ~76.75% LTV with the canary operator grant (v1 stack).
entries.proves: A dedicated, permissioned canary profile lets the keeper keep a real position just under the liquidation line.

entries.summary: First liquidation on the v1 stack: the team canary liquidated through the FlashLiquidator with zero capital (749k gas).
entries.proves: Zero-capital liquidation works on Mezo’s Morpho. Mezo estimated 477k gas; the keeper now sends 2× with a 2M floor (finding K-1).

entries.summary: Keeper’s v1 canary repaid and closed with one repayAndWithdraw when the keeper moved to the v2 stack.
entries.proves: The v1 deployment was retired cleanly: no open keeper position was left behind on the pre-audit contracts.

entries.summary: wsMUSD seeded with 1 MUSD of dead shares, deposited into the real sMUSD.
entries.proves: The ERC-4626 wrapper composes with Mezo's live claim-based sMUSD and is protected against first-depositor inflation.

entries.summary: BorrowAccountFactory deployed; its constructor deploys the bcBTC receipt and the BorrowAccount implementation.
entries.proves: The account factory, gated collateral receipt and clone implementation fit in one transaction under Mezo's 10M block gas limit.

entries.summary: M1 created on Mezo's official testnet Morpho Blue: MUSD loan, bcBTC collateral, BtcMusdOracle, AdaptiveCurveIrm, LLTV 0.77.
entries.proves: A redemption-free BTC→MUSD market now exists on Mezo's own Morpho deployment, created permissionlessly.

entries.summary: Team supplied 3,000 MUSD of liquidity to M1.
entries.proves: Judges can borrow immediately; vMUSD now tops this liquidity up through its allocator.

entries.summary: openAndBorrow: 0.001 BTC sent as msg.value, 30 MUSD borrowed in one transaction (0.1% origination fee).
entries.proves: One-transaction BTC→MUSD credit priced by the live Skip precompile, with no 2,000-MUSD minimum and no redemption queue.

entries.summary: repayAndWithdraw: debt repaid exactly by shares, collateral withdrawn and unwrapped to native BTC in one transaction.
entries.proves: The oracle-free exit path works on-chain; debt and collateral are both zero afterwards.

entries.summary: Judge journey (e2e harness, real signing wallet): claimed 25 test MUSD from the dispenser in the Get test funds card.
entries.proves: The faucet top-up a judge needs for interest and the fee works from the UI.

entries.summary: Judge journey: one MUSD permit signature, then depositWithPermit put 5 MUSD into wsMUSD (5 shares) in one transaction.
entries.proves: The Save flow needs no separate approval for EOAs: permit and deposit land together on Mezo testnet.

entries.summary: Judge journey: redeemInKind burned the remaining 3 wsMUSD for 3 sMUSD sent straight to the wallet.
entries.proves: wsMUSD’s exit that bypasses sMUSD deposits and withdrawals works on the live sMUSD.

entries.summary: Judge journey: one permit, then repayAndWithdrawWithPermit repaid 21.76 MUSD and returned 0.0009 native BTC.
entries.proves: The oracle-free, one-transaction exit works from the UI with a MUSD permit, to the wei.

entries.summary: vMUSD created through Mezo’s own VaultV2Factory (Morpho Vault V2, MUSD asset).
entries.proves: The lending vault is a standard Morpho Vault V2 instance that Mezo’s factory recognises.

entries.summary: WsMusdLiquidityAdapter deployed: vMUSD’s liquidity adapter that parks idle MUSD in wsMUSD.
entries.proves: Deposits earn sMUSD yield until borrowers need the MUSD, and a full wsMUSD cannot block deposits.

entries.summary: BaserateAllocator deployed: no owner, a 2,000 MUSD / 15% M1 buffer, at most 1,000 MUSD per move, 1-hour cooldown.
entries.proves: Allocation follows a fixed public policy anyone can trigger, inside the curator’s caps.

entries.summary: vMUSD seeded with 100 MUSD of dead shares, allocated straight into wsMUSD by the liquidity adapter.
entries.proves: The vault is inflation-protected and the deposit → wsMUSD path works on the live contracts.

entries.summary: Deployer’s temporary allocator role removed; adapter, cap, allocator and fee changes put behind a 48-hour timelock.
entries.proves: Only BaserateAllocator can move vMUSD funds; adapter and cap changes are visible two days ahead.

entries.summary: 3,000 MUSD deposited into vMUSD (3,000 vMUSD minted); the liquidity adapter moved it into wsMUSD in the same call.
entries.proves: Lenders get vMUSD 1:1 and their MUSD earns sMUSD yield from the first block.

entries.summary: First permissionless rebalance: BUFFER_TOP_UP moved 1,000 MUSD from wsMUSD into M1 (M1 liquidity was 876 vs a 2,000 target).
entries.proves: The allocator keeps borrowers’ M1 buffer filled from the vault without any privileged key.

entries.summary: Backstop (bMUSD) deployed: an ERC-4626 over MUSD that buys seized BTC at the oracle price less half the 7.41% incentive.
entries.proves: Liquidations have a buyer of last resort on testnet that does not depend on DEX depth.

entries.summary: FlashLiquidator deployed, bound to M1 and the backstop, with the vAMM venue and a 6.89% maximum price impact.
entries.proves: Anyone can liquidate M1 with zero capital: the seized BTC is sold inside Morpho’s callback.

entries.summary: Backstop seeded with 1 MUSD of dead shares, parked in wsMUSD.
entries.proves: The backstop is live, protected against first-depositor inflation, and earns sMUSD yield on idle cash.

entries.summary: openCanary: 0.002 BTC posted and 123.47 MUSD borrowed at ≈76.7% LTV against the 77% LLTV (CANARY profile).
entries.proves: A live position sits one small BTC dip from liquidation, so the liquidation path can be exercised on real state.

entries.summary: FeeRouter deployed: an ownerless 40/40/20 splitter to sMUSD yield, the testnet BTC/MUSD gauge’s bribe and the treasury.
entries.proves: The bribe target was checked against PoolsVoter.gaugeToBribe at construction; the split cannot be changed.

entries.summary: Governor submitted setFeeRecipient(FeeRouter) on the factory; executable after the 48-hour timelock (27 Oct 19:02 UTC).
entries.proves: Fee changes go through the factory’s public timelock: anyone can see them coming two days ahead.

entries.summary: distribute(): 20 MUSD split into an 8 MUSD bribe on the BTC/MUSD gauge for epoch 1792627200, 8 MUSD to sMUSD, 4 to treasury.
entries.proves: Fees reach veBTC voters (claimable after the Thursday flip) and sMUSD holders through Mezo’s own contracts.

entries.summary: RiskLens deployed: one eth_call returns oracle, market, caps, backstop, depth quotes and the trove queue.
entries.proves: The Risk page reads everything from one stateless contract within Mezo’s precompile limit.
